steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' library.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports to use React and state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building the checkout state recovery flow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create CheckoutRecovery component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CheckoutRecovery that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name CheckoutRecovery that returns null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create CheckoutRecovery component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The CheckoutRecovery component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: A component named CheckoutRecovery is created and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the CheckoutRecovery component. This is the foundation for building the checkout recovery flow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named CheckoutRecovery that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your component definition. You need to create a component named CheckoutRecovery that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize checkout state
steps.instruction: Inside your CheckoutRecovery component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'checkout' initialized with an object containing items (an empty array), total (0), and status ('pending').
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial object: { items: [], total: 0, status: 'pending' } and destructure the returned array into 'checkout' and 'setCheckout'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization for a shopping cart
const [cart, setCart] = useState({ items: [], total: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a 'checkout' state variable initialized with default checkout data.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with the initial object { items: [], total: 0, status: 'pending' } and destructured into 'checkout' and 'setCheckout'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the checkout state with default values.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the exact initial object structure: { items: [], total: 0, status: 'pending' }.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using useState inside the component and initializing it with the required object properties.

steps.title: Initialize recovery state
steps.instruction: Inside the CheckoutRecovery component, use useState to create a state variable named recoveryAttempts initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Add another useState call after your existing checkout state. The pattern is: const [recoveryAttempts, setRecoveryAttempts] = useState(0);
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two state variables: one for checkout data and one for tracking recovery attempts.
successCriteria: A recoveryAttempts state variable is declared using useState and initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up state to track recovery attempts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named recoveryAttempts with initial value 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The recoveryAttempts state variable isn't properly initialized. Check that you're using useState with the correct name and initial value.

steps.title: Define loadCheckoutData function
steps.instruction: Inside your CheckoutRecovery component, define a function named loadCheckoutData that retrieves saved checkout data from localStorage and updates the checkout state if found.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.getItem('checkoutData') to retrieve the saved data, then parse it with JSON.parse() and update the checkout state using setCheckout.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a loadCheckoutData function inside your component that can retrieve and parse saved checkout data from localStorage.
successCriteria: The loadCheckoutData function is defined, retrieves data from localStorage, parses it, and updates the checkout state if data exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the loadCheckoutData function that can recover checkout data from localStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the function, but make sure it retrieves data from localStorage, parses it, and updates the checkout state when data exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a function named loadCheckoutData that gets data from localStorage and updates the checkout state.

steps.title: Define saveCheckoutData function
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named saveCheckoutData that saves the current checkout state to localStorage.
steps.hint: Use localStorage.setItem with a key like 'checkoutData' and JSON.stringify to store the checkout state object.
steps.expectedOutcome: A saveCheckoutData function is defined that can persist the checkout state to localStorage.
successCriteria: The saveCheckoutData function is defined, uses localStorage.setItem, and stringifies the checkout state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a function to save checkout data for recovery.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it uses localStorage.setItem and JSON.stringify on the checkout state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't save the checkout state to localStorage correctly.

steps.title: Define attemptRecovery function
steps.instruction: Inside your CheckoutRecovery component, define a function named attemptRecovery that increments the recoveryAttempts count and calls loadCheckoutData.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the recovery state to track attempts and triggers data loading.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named attemptRecovery is defined that updates recovery state and calls loadCheckoutData.
successCriteria: The attemptRecovery function increments recoveryAttempts and calls loadCheckoutData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the recovery function that will track attempts and load saved data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function both updates the recovery state and calls loadCheckoutData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The attemptRecovery function should update recovery state to track attempts and call loadCheckoutData.

steps.title: Add main container and title
steps.instruction: In your CheckoutRecovery component, return a div container with an h1 element displaying 'Checkout Recovery'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement (return null) with a div containing an h1 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic UI structure with a container div and a title heading.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element containing an h1 element with the text 'Checkout Recovery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the main container and title, creating the basic UI structure for the checkout recovery flow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div with an h1 inside it, and the h1 should display 'Checkout Recovery'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div containing an h1 element with the text 'Checkout Recovery'. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Display checkout status and items
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your CheckoutRecovery component, add a <div> that displays the checkout status, item count, and total from the checkout state. Use the existing checkout state variable.
steps.hint: You can display the checkout items count with checkout.items.length and the total with checkout.total. Use JSX curly braces to embed these values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current checkout status with item count and total amount when the component renders.
successCriteria: A <div> element is added inside the return statement that displays checkout.items.length and checkout.total values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the checkout state in the UI. Users can now see the current item count and total amount.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some checkout display, but make sure to show both the item count (checkout.items.length) and total amount (checkout.total).
steps.feedbackWrong: The checkout status isn't displayed correctly. Check that you're using the checkout state variable and displaying both item count and total.

steps.title: Add recovery button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button with the text 'Attempt Recovery' inside the main container, and wire its onClick event to call the attemptRecovery function. Also display the recovery.attempted status in the UI.
steps.hint: Create a button element with an onClick handler that calls attemptRecovery. You can also add a paragraph to show whether recovery has been attempted.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Attempt Recovery' appears in the UI, and clicking it triggers the attemptRecovery function. The recovery attempt status is displayed.
successCriteria: Button with 'Attempt Recovery' text and onClick handler calling attemptRecovery is added. Recovery status (recovery.attempted) is displayed in the UI.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the recovery button and wired it to the attemptRecovery function. The UI now shows the recovery attempt status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the button, but make sure the onClick handler correctly calls attemptRecovery and the recovery status is displayed.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or onClick handler is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add a button with text 'Attempt Recovery' and onClick={attemptRecovery}, and display recovery.attempted.

lessonTitle: Build resilient checkout state recovery flow
